To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

high concentrations of plasminogen-activator inhibitor-1 and a decreased ratio of tissue-type plasmino-gen activator to urokinase type plasminogen acti-vator in tracheal-aspirate fluid are associated with the development of bronchopulmonary-dysplasia and with the severity of respiratory-distress syndrome among preterm infants.

high concentrations of PAI-I and an increased ratio PAI-1/uPA, with a concomitantly less increased ratio PAI-I/tPA, are associated in preterm infants with the severity of the respiratory distress syndrome ( RDS ) during the first post-natal days.

high concentrations of PAI1 and increased ratios of PAI1 to uPA are associated with the degree of respiratory distress syndrome among preterm infants in the early postnatal period and may play a pathophysiologically important role in the development and persistence of bronchopulmonarydysplasia.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the pathophysiologic mechanisms of respiratory distress syndrome in preterm infants and its sequelae.
the development of new methods for the treatment of respiratory failure and pulmonary hypertension, as well as the development of a new method for the treatment of pulmonary hypertension.
the role of plasminogen activation in the pathophysiology of respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) of the newborn.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the PAI-1/tPA and PAI-1/uPA ratios were significantly elevated in the tracheal aspirates of infants with RDS who subsequently developed BPD.
PAI-1 is a key player in the development of RDS and BPD.
high concentrations of PAI1 in the lungs of preterm babies with RDS is associated with a higher risk of BPD.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the lungs of preterm neonates with respiratory distress syndrome ( RDS) contain high concentrations of PAI-I and that this is associated with a poor prognosis.
the inhibition of intra-alveolar fibrinolytic system is a pathophysiological feature of RDS.
PAI-1 is a major regulator of fibrinolysin in the lungs of preterm neonates with RDS, and its high concentrations may contribute to the development of BDP.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the high concentrations of PAI‐1 in the lungs of preterm newborns are associated with the development and severity of RDS and that the increased ratio of PA1‐1 to uPA is related to a concurrent decrease in the ratio of PAI‐I to tPA.

the lungs of preterm newborns with respiratory distress syndrome (hyaline membrane disease) have high levels of a protein that inhibits fibrinolysis, which may contribute to the severity of the disease.
PAI-1 may play an important role in the pathogenesis of RDS.
